findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted
findings.description:
The line changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which drops the negation.
- **Billing enabled:** the org now gets both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` (line 153), so it is published immediately. This bypasses the unpublished-until-paid flow that `packages/features/ee/teams/api/upgrade.ts:45-66` relies on.
- **Billing disabled (self-hosted):** the org gets neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`, so it has no slug at all.

This is unrelated to the destination-calendar feature and looks like an accidental logic flip inside a style rewrite. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`.

findings.title: Unguarded dereference of `mainHostDestinationCalendar` in `EventManager.create`
findings.description:
`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar (`null` from `handleNewBooking.ts:1067`, or `[]` from the other call sites). The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining.

A Google Meet booking for a user with no destination calendar now throws a `TypeError`. That is exactly the case this fallback exists for; the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` switched it to Cal Video. TypeScript does not catch it because array destructuring is typed as non-undefined. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store `credentialId`
findings.description:
The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so every non-calendar (video) reference is persisted without a credential.
- `createMeeting` does return it (`packages/core/videoClient.ts:78`).
- `handleCancelBooking.ts:491` only calls `deleteMeeting` when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set.

Video meetings for newly created bookings will therefore not be deleted on cancellation. Use `result.credentialId` for both branches.

findings.title: Google Calendar fallbacks are dead code or regress to the wrong calendar
findings.description:
- **`updateEvent` (254-256) and `deleteEvent` (315-317):** the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match. Previously it fell back to the destination calendar's `externalId`. `updateEvent` now sends `calendarId: undefined`; `deleteEvent` always falls to `"primary"`.
- **`createEvent` patch (168):** `events.insert` uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"` (154), but the follow-up `events.patch` passes raw `selectedCalendar`, which is `undefined` when no credential matched. The hangout-link description patch then targets no calendar.
- **Legacy destinations without `credentialId` (147-149):** `EventManager.ts:375-381` matches credentials by type, but the `find` on `cal.credentialId === credentialId` never matches, so the event lands in `"primary"` instead of the chosen calendar. The same branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without `externalId`, so the reference stores `externalCalendarId: undefined`.

findings.title: `updateLocation` references lose `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`
findings.description:
References are now built from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. For calendar results these come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, whose return object (`packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-322`) contains neither field.

`editLocation.handler.ts:120` then persists new calendar references with both values undefined, where they previously came from `evt.destinationCalendar`. A later cancel or reschedule of that booking drops into the legacy no-credential path. Return `externalId` and `credentialId` from `updateEvent`, or keep deriving them from the reference.

findings.title: `updateAllCalendarEvents` swallows errors and under-handles multiple references
findings.description:
- **Silent catch:** `console.error(message)` was removed, but `message` is still built at lines 592-595 and never used. Failures now return `success: false` placeholders with no log.
- **Possibly undefined credential (542):** if the new DB fallback finds nothing, `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is called with `undefined`. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` then throws on `credential.appName`; the promise is returned un-awaited via `Promise.all(result)`, so the surrounding `catch` does not handle it. Guard with `if (!credential) continue`, as `createAllCalendarEvents` does at line 369.
- **Merge path (554):** still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so only the first old calendar event is deleted. Other hosts' old events are orphaned now that there can be several references.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services use the first host's calendar with every host's credential
findings.description:
`EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent` once per destination with that host's credential. Only Google selects the calendar by `credentialId`. These services always take `destinationCalendar[0]`:
- Office365 `createEvent`
- Lark `createEvent`, `createAttendees`, `updateEvent`, `deleteEvent`
- `BaseCalendarService` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-165`)

For a collective event whose second host uses one of these, the request goes out with host B's credential against host A's calendar id. It will fail or create nothing. Either pass and use `credentialId` in these services too, or limit the multi-destination loop to integrations that support it.

findings.title: Team destination calendars dropped when the organizer has none
findings.description:
`evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so the other collective hosts' calendars are silently discarded.

The empty value is also inconsistent: `null` here, `[]` at every other call site in this diff. `webhook.e2e.ts` now expects `null` at lines 119 and 373 but `[]` at line 249 for the same payload field. Initialise to `[]` here. Separately, pushing into `teamDestinationCalendars` from inside the `teamMemberPromises` map callback (lines 990-994) is a hidden side effect; a plain filter/map over `users.slice(1)` would be clearer.

findings.title: Unrelated `loadUsers` rewrite changes behaviour and error semantics
findings.description:
This refactor is outside the feature's scope and changes behaviour:
- The `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` select was dropped for dynamic users, though the hosts query at 321-325 still selects it and `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) declares it.
- The `|| []` fallback on `eventType.users` (line 755) was removed, yet line 770 immediately calls `users.some`.
- An empty `dynamicUserList` now throws a plain `Error`, which the catch converts to a generic 500 "Unable to load users" with the cause discarded and nothing logged.
- Any `HttpError` is rethrown as 400 regardless of its original status.
- `Array.isArray(hosts)` after `|| []` is a dead check.
- The `// Don't leak to client` comment on `credentials: true` was removed.

findings.title: Cancel loop repeats recurring deletions per reference; credential lookup duplicated
findings.description:
The recurring-event branch now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, but it ignores `reference`. It iterates all of the user's calendar credentials across all `updatedBookings`, so with N calendar references the same delete calls run N times. It also still uses `updBooking.references.find(...)` and only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, so other hosts' events for recurring collective bookings are not removed. Hoist that branch out of the loop.

Separately, the "fetch credential from DB and map to `CredentialWithAppName`" block is copy-pasted at `packages/core/EventManager.ts:344-367` and `517-540`, and both run sequential `findUnique` queries inside a loop. Extract a helper.

findings.title: No tests for the new multi-destination behaviour
findings.description:
The only test change is one expected payload value flipping from `null` to `[]`. No `*.test.ts` file in the repo references `handleNewBooking`, `EventManager` or `destinationCalendar`. Nothing covers:
- per-host event creation for collective bookings
- credential fallback from the DB
- multi-reference update and cancel
- Google calendar selection by `credentialId`

The defects above (null dereference, lost video `credentialId`, dead fallbacks) are the kind a basic unit test of `EventManager.create` would catch.

findings.title: Enum comparisons replaced with string literals
findings.description: `SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE` / `SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN` comparisons became `["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(...)`, and `=== "COLLECTIVE"` at lines 992 and 1077. This loses compile-time checking for no functional gain. The `isTeamEventType &&` guard at 992 and 1077 is also redundant with the `COLLECTIVE` check.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape changes for consumers
findings.description: `destinationCalendar` in `CalendarEvent` is serialised into webhook payloads, as the e2e expectation change shows. It is now an array instead of an object or `null`, which is a breaking change for external webhook consumers and should be called out in release notes.

findings.title: Mechanical array wrapping at call sites is consistent with the new type
findings.description: The wrapping in `bookingReminder.ts`, the payment webhooks, `confirm`/`editLocation`/`requestReschedule`/`deleteCredential` handlers, `BrokenIntegrationEmail.tsx` and `class.ts` matches `DestinationCalendar[] | null`. A repo-wide grep for single-object access (`destinationCalendar?.externalId`, `.integration`, `.credentialId`) found only Prisma user/event-type objects, not `CalendarEvent`. The `requestReschedule` change also removes a redundant `a || a` expression.
